page: Amazon Web Services c6in.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test of 1880.89 and Geekbench single-core score of 1565.0, fall within the average category. However, due to the low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core at 1920.38 and Geekbench multi-core at 1810.0, both scoring in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 13.88 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 12.88 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%.

The c6in.large instance is designed for network and EBS-optimized workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles but modest memory footprints. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Given its hardware profile, it is suitable for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, and small-scale utility processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its weak performance in 135M model text generation and poor database operations score.
